## Constrained least squares for the reaction extents (`leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin`) {#sec-ch04-active-set}

### Summary

Each step of both solvers asks for reaction extents that reduce the saturation deficits of the active reactions,
without making any mole fraction or concentration negative. That is a linear least-squares problem with inequality
constraints. kintera solves it with an active-set method on the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions: it keeps a
working set of constraints held as equalities, drops every working constraint whose multiplier is negative, adds the
most violated independent one, and stops when the working set no longer changes. The standard theory of such methods
is in the literature;[^ch04-active-set-refs] the general solver and its scaling are described in @sec-ch10-kkt.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Solve @eq-ch04-active-set-problem for the extents of one outer step.

**Data.** Gain matrix, deficits, stoichiometry, current amounts; extents out.

**Placement.** Step 4 of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp and step 3 of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv.

**Activation.** Always, when at least one reaction is active.

**Guarantee / limits.** Returns codes 0-3; a constraint dependent on the working set is not enforced.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf A$ the gain matrix $\mathsf W\mathsf S$ of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp; $\mathbf b$ the deficits;
$\mathsf C$ the constraint matrix; $\mathbf d$ the current amounts (mole fractions or concentrations); $f$ the
objective $\tfrac12\lVert\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b\rVert_2^2$; $\boldsymbol\mu$ the multipliers of the
constraint rows; $\mathcal W$ the working set, the rows held as equalities.

### Derivation

A step of extents $\boldsymbol\xi$ changes the amounts by $\mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi$. Requiring every new amount to be
non-negative, $\mathbf d + \mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi \ge 0$, is the same as $-\mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi \le \mathbf d$.
The step is therefore the solution of

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\boldsymbol\xi}\ \ & \lVert \mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b \rVert_2 , \\
\mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi &\le \mathbf d , \\
\mathsf C &= -\mathsf S .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-active-set-problem}

Because $\mathbf d$ holds the current amounts, which are non-negative, $\boldsymbol\xi = 0$ is feasible. The solver
relies on that and checks it on entry, accepting $d_i \ge -64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\max_j |d_j|$ so that the
rounding residue of a used-up stock still counts as zero.

**Step 1: the optimality conditions.** Minimising $\lVert\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b\rVert_2$ and minimising
$f(\boldsymbol\xi) = \tfrac12\lVert\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b\rVert_2^2$ give the same $\boldsymbol\xi$. The
function $f$ is a convex quadratic, with gradient $\nabla f = \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b)$
and Hessian $\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A$, which is positive semidefinite. Give each inequality row $i$ a multiplier
$\mu_i$ and form the Lagrangian

$$
\mathcal L(\boldsymbol\xi, \boldsymbol\mu) = \tfrac12\lVert\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf b\rVert_2^2
  + \boldsymbol\mu^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf d) .
$$

The constraints are linear, so the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions are necessary at a minimum without any further
qualification. Because $f$ is convex they are also sufficient, and any point that satisfies them is a global
minimum:[^ch04-active-set-kkt-refs]

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) stationarity:} && \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A\,\boldsymbol\xi + \mathsf C^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\mu
  = \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf b , \\
&\text{(ii) primal feasibility:} && \mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi \le \mathbf d , \\
&\text{(iii) dual feasibility:} && \boldsymbol\mu \ge 0 , \\
&\text{(iv) complementarity:} && \mu_i\,(\mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi - \mathbf d)_i = 0 \ \text{for every row } i .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-active-set-kkt}

Condition (i) is $\partial\mathcal L/\partial\boldsymbol\xi = 0$. Condition (iv) says that a row that is not tight,
$(\mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi)_i < d_i$, has $\mu_i = 0$. So only tight rows (species driven exactly to zero) carry a
multiplier.

**Step 2: the working-set system.** If we knew which rows are tight at the solution, we could hold those rows as
equalities, set the multipliers of the others to zero, and (i)–(iv) would reduce to a linear system. Call the guessed
set of tight rows the working set $\mathcal W$, with rows $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$, bounds $\mathbf d_{\mathcal W}$ and
multipliers $\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W}$. Conditions (i) and "row $i \in \mathcal W$ is tight" give

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A & \mathsf C_{\mathcal W}^{\mathsf T} \\
  \mathsf C_{\mathcal W} & 0 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \boldsymbol\xi \\ \boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf b \\ \mathbf d_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix} .
$$ {#eq-ch04-active-set-block}

This block matrix is non-singular when $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$ has independent rows and $\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A$
is positive definite on the directions that keep the working rows tight, the null space of $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$.
The first requirement is why only independent rows may enter $\mathcal W$ (Step 5). The second holds whenever the gain
$\mathsf A$ is non-singular. The solution of @eq-ch04-active-set-block satisfies (i) and (iv) by construction. It is
the answer if it also satisfies (ii) for the rows outside $\mathcal W$ and (iii) for the rows inside. The working-set
iteration repairs whichever of these fails.

**Step 3: what a negative multiplier means.** Let $(\boldsymbol\xi, \boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W})$ solve
@eq-ch04-active-set-block, with $\mu_i < 0$ for some $i \in \mathcal W$. Take a direction $\mathbf p$ that keeps the
other working rows tight, $(\mathsf C\mathbf p)_j = 0$ for $j \in \mathcal W$, $j \ne i$, and moves off row $i$ into
the feasible side, $(\mathsf C\mathbf p)_i < 0$. Such a direction exists because the working rows are independent. By
(i), the rate of change of $f$ along $\mathbf p$ is

$$
\nabla f^{\mathsf T}\mathbf p = (\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi - \mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf b)^{\mathsf T}\mathbf p
  = -\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W}^{\mathsf T}\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}\mathbf p = -\mu_i\,(\mathsf C\mathbf p)_i < 0 .
$$

So the objective decreases when the species of row $i$ is allowed to be positive again: holding it at zero was a
mistake, and the row is released. With $\mu_i \ge 0$ the same product is $\ge 0$ for every feasible direction, and the
bound is genuinely holding the solution. In the same way, $\mu_i$ is the rate at which the minimum of $f$ falls as the
bound $d_i$ is loosened, $\partial f_{\min}/\partial d_i = -\mu_i$.

**Step 4: the direct form for a square gain.** Both callers pass a square $\mathsf A$ (one row per active reaction).
The block of @eq-ch04-active-set-block contains $\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A$, whose condition number is the square
of that of $\mathsf A$, because its singular values are the squares of those of $\mathsf A$. When $\mathsf A$ is
non-singular, multiply the first block row by $\mathsf A^{-\mathsf T}$:
$\mathsf A^{-\mathsf T}(\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A\boldsymbol\xi + \mathsf C_{\mathcal W}^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W})
= \mathsf A^{-\mathsf T}\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf b$ gives

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathsf A & \mathsf A^{-\mathsf T}\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}^{\mathsf T} \\
  \mathsf C_{\mathcal W} & 0 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \boldsymbol\xi \\ \boldsymbol\mu_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf b \\ \mathbf d_{\mathcal W} \end{bmatrix} ,
$$ {#eq-ch04-active-set-direct}

with the same unknowns and multipliers, and a conditioning that follows $\mathsf A$ rather than its square.
`kkt_solve_direct` ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h kkt_solve_direct >}}) forms
$\mathsf A^{-\mathsf T}\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}^{\mathsf T}$ column by column from an LU factorisation of
$\mathsf A^{\mathsf T}$. It works on the scaled matrices of @sec-ch10-kkt: columns are divided by their largest entry,
the right side by the largest $|b_i|$, and each constraint row by its largest scaled entry or $|d_i|$.

**Step 5: dependent rows.** A row whose scaled vector lies within $\sqrt{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}}$ of the span of
the working rows would make $\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$ nearly rank-deficient. The multipliers would then lose all their
digits, since the block's condition number grows like the inverse square of the smallest singular value of
$\mathsf C_{\mathcal W}$. Such a row is never added. There is one row per species but only one unknown per active
reaction, so the rows are dependent whenever there are more species than active reactions. For example, take ammonia shared by ammonia ice (extent $\xi_1$) and ammonium hydrosulfide ($\xi_2$). The
non-negativity rows of ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and the two condensates are $(1, 1)$, $(0, 1)$, $(-1, 0)$ and
$(0, -1)$ in the unknowns $(\xi_1, \xi_2)$. At most two of them can be independent, so a third violated row cannot be
held. The returned step may then violate it, and both callers clip each reaction's extent to the stock of the species
it consumes.

**Step 6: the constraint in amounts.** With $\mathsf C = -\mathsf S$ and $\mathbf d = \mathbf x$ (mole fractions at
fixed $T, p$, concentrations at fixed $U, V$), row $i$ of $\mathsf C\boldsymbol\xi \le \mathbf d$ reads
$-(\mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi)_i \le x_i$, that is $x_i + (\mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi)_i \ge 0$: the amount of species $i$
after the step is not negative. The callers build $\mathsf C$ by negating the active columns of the stoichiometry
matrix in place (`stoich_active` in `equilibrate_tp`). @eq-ch04-active-set-problem is assembled in `equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}) and solved by `leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin`
({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin >}}).

### Numerical method

`leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin` ({{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin >}}) iterates:

1. **Solve with the working set as equalities.** When $\mathsf A$ is square it first tries the KKT system in a direct
   form, which avoids squaring the condition number. On a zero pivot or a non-finite solution it falls back to the
   normal equations with a small diagonal regularisation.
2. **Drop.** Every working inequality whose multiplier is negative is removed, all in one pass.
3. **Add.** Of the constraints the current solution violates, it adds the single most violated one that is linearly
   independent of the working set: the part of its scaled row orthogonal to the working rows must keep more than
   $\sqrt{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}}$ of its norm. This keeps the working set full rank when several rows share a
   direction, for example two condensates drawing on one vapour.
4. **Stop** when the working set is the same as in the previous iteration. With independent rows this means that no
   multiplier is negative and no constraint is violated. A violated row that depends on the working set is never
   added, so the loop can also stop with such a row still violated.

A violated constraint that depends linearly on the working set is never added, so the returned step may still violate
it. That is why both solvers clip each reaction's extent to its reactants' stock afterwards. A working constraint with a
single non-zero coefficient is a bound on one unknown, and the solution is returned exactly on it.

@fig-ch04-active-set-loop gives the order of the steps.

#| fig-alt: "Five boxes left to right: working set as equalities, solve the KKT system, drop every row with a negative multiplier, add the most violated independent row, stop when the working set is unchanged; an arrow loops from the add step back to the solve."

| general solver (all violated rows at once) | {{< code src/math/leastsq_kkt.h leastsq_kkt >}} | `leastsq_kkt` | not used by these solvers |

: Code map of the constrained least-squares step. {#tbl-ch04-active-set-code}

The return codes are 0 on success; 1 on invalid input or when $\boldsymbol\xi = 0$ is not feasible; 2 when the
iteration bound is reached; 3 when the KKT system stays singular, or when a solve that needed the regularised fallback
ends with a working row that does not hold. After such a solve the code checks every working row, scaled as in
@sec-ch10-kkt, against $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} + 10\,r$, with $r$ the fallback regularisation, and returns 3 if
one misses it. The bound is the larger of the number of species
plus one and `max-iter`. A non-zero code ends the outer solve, which then reports it through the diagnostic
(@sec-ch04-warm-start-failures).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_alloc_space.release` | the workspace size of the solvers | exact | byte counts |
| `test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` | dependent rows: two condensates sharing a vapour stay non-negative and atom-conserving | `rtol=1e-12` (N, S); RH within $10^{-5}$ | not stated in the test |

: Tests of the constrained least-squares step. {#tbl-ch04-active-set-tests}

No test in the tree calls the solver directly. Its dependent-constraint policy is exercised by an existing test:
`test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` uses two condensates that share a vapour (ammonia ice and ammonium
hydrosulfide), so each step has two reaction extents and four non-negativity rows, any three of them linearly
dependent, as the test's docstring states. It requires every adjusted cell to be non-negative, unsupersaturated and
atom-conserving, and it passes in both builds of @sec-ch13-results, on the CPU device.

The derivation check is indirect as well. `check_ch4_tp.py` line a runs the fixed-temperature solver on
`tests/jupiter.yaml`, where ammonia is shared by ammonia ice and ammonium hydrosulfide, which are the dependent rows of
Step 5. At 200 and 160 K, with ammonium hydrosulfide present, the conditions of @sec-ch04-conditions hold to
$6.95\times10^{-8}$ (tolerance $10^{-6}$), and nitrogen and sulfur change by at most $3.3\times10^{-16}$ (relative,
tolerance $10^{-14}$). The line does not assert non-negativity; the condensate amounts it prints are non-negative
(run record in @sec-ch04-conditions).

A direct test is proposed, not present: a C++ test that calls `leastsq_kkt_feasible_origin` on a problem with a
closed-form KKT solution. For $\mathsf A = \mathsf I_2$, $\mathbf b = (1, -1)$ and the single row $-\xi_2 \le 1/2$,
the unconstrained minimum $(1, -1)$ violates the row. By @eq-ch04-active-set-kkt the answer is
$\boldsymbol\xi = (1, -1/2)$ with $\mu = 1/2$. Adding the dependent row $-2\xi_2 \le 1$, the same bound written twice, must leave the answer
unchanged with only one of the two rows in the working set. Adding a row that is tight at the start, $\xi_1 \le 0$ with $d = 0$, exercises
the feasible-origin check and gives $\boldsymbol\xi = (0, -1/2)$.

[^ch04-active-set-kkt-refs]: [source: J. Nocedal and S. J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., Springer (2006),
<https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5>, section 12.3 (first-order conditions; linear constraints satisfy the
constraint qualification), section 16.1 (non-singularity of the equality-constrained block) and section 16.5
(active-set methods for convex quadratic programs, including the meaning of a negative multiplier).]

[^ch04-active-set-refs]: [source: J. Nocedal and S. J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., Springer (2006),
<https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-40065-5>, chapter 16; C. L. Lawson and R. J. Hanson, Solving Least Squares
Problems, SIAM (1995), <https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611971217>, chapter 23.]

### Limits

- Constraints dependent on the working set are not enforced (see above); the caller's clip covers them.
- On a near-singular gain matrix the regularised fallback is used. The code then checks that the working rows hold
  (feasibility), as above; it does not check how close the objective is to its minimum, and that is not measured.
